purpose: C2: blast-radius coverage vs a frozen labeled impacted-set (PLAN.md gate: coverage > 0.90, measured graph traversal vs manual ground truth).
question: Given a changed entity/hunk, does VerifyCI identify the entities actually exposed by the change?
provenance: Fixture `fixture/src/core.py` + `src/app.py` encode a hand-annotated CALLS topology (hub -> mid1/mid2 -> leaf; far/remote/handle -> hub; isolated leafless). Expected impacted sets are derived BY HAND from that topology + the documented contract (2 hops, incoming+outgoing along CALL_FLOW_TYPES={CALLS,REFERENCES,IMPORTS,INHERITS,DEPENDS_ON}, seed excluded) BEFORE any blast computation. `author.py` regenerates cases.jsonl byte-identically.
labels_are_data: expected_impacted was fixed before detection; misses are reported, never retuned. Traversal was NOT repaired for the tail-insertion gap.
detection_path: identical to the gate: parse_diff_files -> seed_entities_for_diff (hunk-line based) -> compute_blast_radius (2 hops, CALL_FLOW_TYPES). Harness adds no retrieval/blast logic.

findings.traversal: EXACT (recall 1.0, FN 0) on every seeded hunk: direct, transitive, multi-path, cross-file, method callee. Zero-impact change correctly returns empty. 2-hop incoming+outgoing confirmed (B1/B4/B9).
findings.tail_insertion_gap: B6 (pure insertion after hub's last line): hunk-line seeding yields changed_entities=[] -> risk 0.0 -> 6 of 6 expected dependents missed. This is the C1 structural gap reproduced as a labeled case, NOT repaired.
findings.precision_artifact: B5 (def-line hunk): the 3 lines of diff context bleed into the adjacent `far` definition, so seed_entities_for_diff yields {hub, far}; far is a real hub caller, and hub then re-enters as far's callee -> detected includes the seed `hub`, an FP vs the contract (seed excluded). Detected set is a strict superset of expected (recall 1.0). Root cause: hunk context-window vs entity-span intersection, not traversal.
findings.note: seeded changed_entities includes PARAMETER rows (x, self); harmless (never traversal seeds) but shows seeding is entity-type-agnostic.

gate_verdict: coverage_all 0.8571 < 0.90 -> NOT MET. But: the ONLY sub-1.0 case is the pre-labeled tail-insertion gap, and that corpus is tiny (7 non-empty cases); coverage_seeded_only 1.0 shows traversal itself is correct. Result is measured, not established; the gap is a documented scope limit, the FP a disclosed seeding artifact.
no_tuning_rule: first run is the baseline; any later seeding/traversal change must re-measure against this frozen corpus and update the recorded constants with a review note, never tune to it.
cap003_review_note: Reviewed re-baseline (CAP-003): post-freeze diffmap commits repaired tail-insertion seeding (span-intersection now attributes B6/B7 hunks to enclosing functions; _is_seedable excludes PARAMETER/IMPORT/VARIABLE). Mode rule frozen independently in cap003_tail_seeding/MODE_PROTOCOL.md (stdlib-ast geometry, no detector code; generator byte-reproducible) BEFORE the promotional measurement: B6/B7 known_gap->seeded. All 9 expected impacted sets re-derived from fixture topology + 2-hop contract and match v1 exactly (B6 = B1 topological twin) — no expected set tuned. Re-measured 9/9 recall 1.0, coverage 1.0/1.0, canonical ESTABLISHED. B5 FP persists as disclosed. v1 1.0/0.8571 preserved in git history + cap003 config frozen_reference.
